title: Pharmacy Override Decision — EHR Downtime

transcript.speaker: Anil Desai
transcript.text: CNO, it's Anil Desai in Pharmacy. The automated dispensing cabinets cannot verify against pharmacy orders, so every pull is stuck waiting. I can put all cabinets into override, which opens the override list on every unit, including opioids and insulin. Or I can keep them locked and send pharmacists to the units. I have 14 pharmacists in the building at 06:10. Tell me which.

transcript.speaker: Carol Beckett
transcript.text: Anil, confirm override mode on all cabinets. We need to maintain medication flow. Use the second-nurse verification for opioids, insulin, and heparin. Send a pharmacist to ICU 3 North, ICU 3 South, the ED, and 6 West immediately. Document every override pull on the paper log and ensure Pharmacy counts all cabinets each shift.

instructorNote: This inject tests the CNO's authority to authorize override mode and ensure medication safety protocols are followed. Watch for coordination between Pharmacy and Nursing to confirm override list access and second-nurse verification for high-alert drugs.
